The variant is SA insured unemployment from regular state programs, not NSA state totals and not all-program continued weeks claimed."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Opened the DOL ETA UI Weekly Claims archive and publication schedule page.","result":"The DOL page says the UI Weekly Claims News Release is published each week on Thursday at 8:30 AM EST, lists Wednesday November 25, 2026 as the 2026 non-Thursday exception, and shows the page was updated July 9, 2026. The last five published levels rose from 1.786 million to 1.814 million, but initial claims for July 4 were 215,000 and the four-week initial-claims average was 218,750, so the near-term pressure is mild rather than a breakout."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence prior = latest official SA insured unemployment of 1.814 million; historical sample = 53 fetched weekly observations from the DOL table, June 28, 2025 through June 27, 2026, yielding 52 successive week-to-week changes; adjustment components = +0.010 million for two weeks of modest recent upward momentum, 0.000 million for policy mechanics because no Extended Benefits trigger was on, and 0.000 million for variant conversion because all anchors use the same SA insured-unemployment variant. Point = 1.814 + 0.010 = 1.824 million. For the fetched weekly changes, sigma = 0.0208 million, so one-week 80% half-width is 1.28*sigma = 0.0266 million. Because the target is two unpublished weeks ahead, I scale by sqrt(2), giving about 0.0376 million, rounded to 0.038 million; interval = 1.824 +/- 0.038 = [1.786, 1.862] million."},{"kind":"text","text":"Level and momentum effects: the latest 1.814 million is above the May 30 level by 0.028 million but still below the comparable prior-year value of 1.952 million. Momentum argues for a small increase, while the latest initial-claims easing to 215,000 limits the upward adjustment."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-considerations: upside risk would come from a delayed follow-through from late-June layoffs or seasonal-adjustment miss that lifts continued claims above 1.862 million. Downside risk would come from faster exits from UI rolls or lower July initial claims that pull the print below 1.786 million. A holiday-week reporting distortion or a large state-level administrative revision would be the main outside the interval scenario."},{"kind":"text","text":"Review disposition: accepted the sample-count clarification, so the interval step now says 53 observations and 52 successive changes; accepted the clarification that FRED is only a history mirror and not the resolution source; left the point, interval, resolver, and source set unchanged."},{"kind":"forecast","point":1.824,"ciLow":1.786,"ciHigh":1.862}]}
